name: Muir
insider_take: This sophisticated harbourfront gem seamlessly blends Nova Scotia's maritime heritage with contemporary luxury, offering front-row seats to one of Canada's most historic and vibrant waterfronts.
whats_special: The Muir stands as Halifax's first Luxury Collection property, occupying a prime position overlooking the famous Halifax Harbour where the Titanic rescue ships once docked. The hotel's design pays homage to the region's Scottish roots and seafaring history, while the harbour views stretch across the same waters that have welcomed ships for over 270 years.
pro_tip: Book a harbour-facing room to witness the daily ballet of navy vessels, cruise ships, and sailing boats—plus catch stunning sunrises over one of the world's largest natural harbours.
dont_miss: Step outside to explore the Halifax Seaport Farmers' Market (North America's oldest continuously operating farmers' market), stroll the historic waterfront boardwalk, or take a short walk to Pier 21—Canada's equivalent to Ellis Island where over one million immigrants first set foot in the country.
pros: Prime waterfront location in Halifax's vibrant downtown core
Luxury Collection elegance with contemporary maritime-inspired design
Access to Marriott STARS Program exclusive benefits and amenities
Modern accommodations with panoramic harbor and city views
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects high-end positioning
Urban setting may not suit guests seeking secluded retreat atmosphere
